title: Top Management Brief: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Chief executive, executive committee, corporate HSE and corporate function heads
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

exclusions.reason: A reviewer voted to downgrade this finding; the Learnings Register leaves it out too.

bottom_line.text: Specifications, change control and emergency isolation rules existed only on paper or not at all for legacy equipment; any site of the same vintage can carry the same gaps.
Protective systems were designed around people reaching the hazard: detection that only displays an alarm and isolation valves that can only be closed by hand at the valve.
Enterprise assurance did not see these conditions: audits recorded compliance without plant data, and overdue recommendations were extended without the approval the procedure required.

items.text: On 24 September 2020 condensate vapour escaped from a seal on a 1986 metering skid at the gas terminal. The cloud spread for about 46 minutes before the first isolation valve was closed by hand, and it ignited at 03:08:15 from a damaged flameproof light fitting [FND-322112EE; FND-CCE6F868; EVD-6414; EVD-6916].

The analysis uses the four HFACS levels: unsafe acts (what people did at the point of work), preconditions (the conditions around them), supervision (how work was planned, checked and corrected) and organisational influences (resources, policy, process and culture). This brief draws on the organisational level only, because that is where enterprise decisions act [FND-B440C1BF; FND-1280E788].

The committee is asked to decide on four enterprise standards (pressure-part specifications, change control in use, emergency isolation, and fire and gas executive action) and to note two matters within function authority (hazardous-area electrical maintenance and audit quality); they are set out under 'Decisions for top management' [FND-23139BF9; FND-F7FE8463; FND-5C7B163D; FND-4458E0C0; FND-1280E788].

rows: LR-01 Lost specifications for legacy pressure-boundary parts, with no owner
Likely at similar sites
Vintage of equipment: any site with original-build meters and flanges whose OEM data is no longer on file
LR-06 Change-control procedure published but not in use
Enterprise-wide
Shared standard: the procedure is a corporate document, so its use is a question for every site
LR-07 Emergency plan without isolation criteria or delegated authority
Enterprise-wide
Shared standard: every major-hazard site writes its emergency plan to the same regulations
LR-09 Emergency isolation valves operable only by hand at the valve
Likely at similar sites
Vintage of equipment: valves installed before remote operation became the expectation
LR-10 Gas detection that only displays an alarm
Likely at similar sites
Shared system: detection set up as annunciation without executive action
LR-11 Breakdown-led maintenance of hazardous-area electrical fittings
Enterprise-wide
Culture: a maintenance philosophy, not a single defect
LR-20 Audits recording compliance without plant data
Enterprise-wide
Shared standard: the audit method and checklists are set centrally

sections.heading: Policies, standards and legal requirements implicated

items.text: The original gasket specification for the 1986 meter was not on file and no role owned it, so locally bought O-rings were used as regular practice with no specification or quality check at purchase. The enterprise spares standard did not reach legacy pressure-boundary parts [FND-23139BF9; FND-6B3A6492; EVD-8645].

The management-of-change procedure was published in August 2016, but no change had gone through it since 2018, including the switch to a different seal. The standard existed; its use was not checked [FND-F7FE8463; EVD-2986].

The site emergency plan named the major hydrocarbon leak as a scenario but gave no criteria for isolation or stoppage and no authority below the plant manager to order it. What the evidence shows is a gap between the scenario and the decision; whether the plan meets the regulations is for the competent authority [FND-5C7B163D; FND-82761CC5; EVD-4052; EVD-3932].

Electrical maintenance of flameproof fittings in the Zone 1 area was breakdown-led, and a fitting with three missing bolts stayed in service until it became the probable ignition source [FND-1280E788; FND-ABF11182; EVD-6916].

No qualification for control-room staff was defined in the HR or operations policy; new staff received a four-day general course and no simulator practice before emergency duties [FND-6CBACB54; FND-268CA069; EVD-5634].

items.group: Audit and corrective action (OISD standards; ISO 45001 9.2 and 10.2)
items.text: The self-safety audit checklist was not specific to the plant and recorded compliance where data was later found incomplete and not in line with OISD standards. Twelve external-audit recommendations from 2018 were extended to April 2021 without the approval the procedure required [FND-9E1AB5BA; FND-2A77BAFB; EVD-9692; EVD-6852].

items.decision: Set one enterprise rule that no critical pressure-boundary part is fitted without a specification and an approved-substitute record, and that one function owns those specifications
options: Mandatory enterprise standard with a stores block on issue
Guidance to sites, checked by audit
items.trade_offs: A stores block stops unspecified parts at the point of issue but needs specifications re-established first for legacy equipment; guidance is quicker to issue and relies on the audit process this event showed did not detect the gap.

items.name: Critical spares with a specification
items.measure: Share of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification and certificate on file, by site
items.deterioration: Any site below the previous quarter, or any part issued without a specification

items.group: For decision: change control in use
items.decision: Require each site to show that its management-of-change procedure is in use, not only published
options: Quarterly MOC activity report with a sampled field check
items.trade_offs: A quarterly report with field sampling finds silent procedures within months but adds reporting load; an annual audit adds less load and leaves a gap of up to a year.

items.group: For decision: change control in use
items.name: MOC activity
items.measure: MOC records opened and closed per site per quarter, and field changes found without a record
items.deterioration: A quarter with no MOC records at an operating site, or any unrecorded change found

items.decision: Set an enterprise standard for emergency isolation: written isolation criteria in every emergency plan, isolation authority delegated to the shift, and remote operation for emergency isolation valves that need access to the hazard area
options: Criteria and delegation first, remote operation by a capital programme
All three together at the highest-risk sites
items.trade_offs: Criteria and delegation can be issued quickly at low cost; remote operation needs capital and shutdown windows, but it is the only option that removes the need to walk into the release.

items.name: Time to isolation in drills
items.measure: Time from a confirmed release to first isolation in drills, by site, and the share of emergency isolation valves operable remotely
items.deterioration: A drill in which isolation waits for authority above the shift, or no change in the remote share over two reporting periods

items.group: For decision: fire and gas executive action
items.decision: Decide whether gas detection at major-hazard sites must trigger automatic shutdown or protection, rather than only display an alarm
options: Executive action at all major-hazard sites
Executive action where a risk study shows manual response is too slow
items.trade_offs: Executive action removes reliance on a manual chain but brings spurious-trip risk and engineering cost; a risk-based approach targets cost but needs a study at each site first.

items.group: For decision: fire and gas executive action
items.name: Detection systems with executive action
items.measure: Share of fire and gas systems at major-hazard sites with defined executive actions, tested in the last test cycle
items.deterioration: Any system found display-only with no recorded risk decision

items.decision: Electrical maintenance of flameproof fittings in hazardous areas moves from breakdown repair to planned inspection, within the maintenance function's authority
options: Planned inspection with recorded condition of each fitting
items.trade_offs: Planned inspection needs crew time and access; the evidence shows breakdown repair left a compromised fitting in service.

items.name: Hazardous-area fittings inspected
items.measure: Share of hazardous-area electrical fittings with a recorded inspection in the planned interval
items.deterioration: Any fitting found with missing fasteners or an open enclosure

items.decision: Audit checklists are written for each plant and filled checklists are retained, within the HSE function's authority
items.trade_offs: Plant-specific checklists take longer to write and audit; generic checklists here recorded compliance without plant data.

items.name: Audit findings re-tested
items.measure: Share of sampled 'compliant' audit findings that an independent re-test confirms
items.deterioration: Any sample in which a 'compliant' finding is not supported by site data

items.question: How will we know the specification, change-control and isolation standards are applied at every site, not only issued?
items.why: At this site each control existed on paper or was assumed, and assurance did not test it.
items.good_evidence: Independent test points sampled at each site (see auditor-assurance-pack), reported to the executive committee with the open items.

items.question: Who approved each extension of an overdue safety recommendation, across all sites?
items.why: Extensions here had no record of the approval the procedure required.
items.good_evidence: A cross-site list of extended recommendations with the approving authority and its record.

gaps.text: [GAP] The export does not show which other sites hold equipment of the same vintage or the same detection and isolation design.
gaps.evidence_needed: An asset register extract by site for legacy metering skids, emergency isolation valves and fire and gas systems.

limits: No finding names corporate leadership directly; the enterprise learnings are drawn from organisational-level findings about the site.
A management-review input table is not included; add it when the brief goes to a management review.
The analysis is a desk review of the published enquiry report; it had no site access or interviews.
